From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acme.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: App integration intake: SDK snippets, endpoint migration windows, and retry/backoff templates

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the details. Below are compact, copy-pasteable examples your engineers can start with. We recommend applying the same retry policy at both client and gateway layers but with slightly different caps (clients: conservative retries, gateway: higher-level throttling).

1) Node (axios) example — timeouts + exponential backoff with jitter:

const axios = require('axios');
const backoff = (retryCount) => Math.min(1000 * Math.pow(2, retryCount), 10000); // ms cap

async function callRedwood(payload, maxRetries = 4) {
  let attempt = 0;
  while (true) {
    try {
      const resp = await axios.post('https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate', payload, {
        timeout: 7000, // 7s socket timeout
        headers: { 'x-request-id': generateRequestId(), 'x-trace-id': generateRequestId() }
      });
      return resp.data;
    } catch (err) {
      if (isRetryable(err) && attempt < maxRetries) {
        const delay = backoff(attempt) * (0.6 + Math.random() * 0.8); // jitter
        await sleep(delay);
        attempt += 1;
        continue;
      }
      throw err;
    }
  }
}

Notes: socket timeout 7s for generation endpoints, shorter for status endpoints (2–3s). Increase timeouts for large batch payloads.

2) cURL example with header guidance:

curl -X POST 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDWOOD_KEY>' \
  -H 'x-request-id: your-uuid-here' \
  -d '{"input": "..."}' --max-time 10

3) Retry policy (ops-friendly):
- Retry on: HTTP 429, 5xx (500, 502, 503, 504), connection reset/timeouts.
- Do NOT retry on: 4xx client errors (400, 401, 403, 404) except 429.
- Max retries: client-side = 3; gateway-side = 6 with token bucket smoothing.
- Backoff: base 500ms, exponential factor 2, cap 10s, full jitter.
- Circuit breaker: open after 12 consecutive failures for 30s, slowly ramp after success.

Trace headers: we recommend x-request-id and x-trace-id; include them in logs to correlate.

Attachment: small sample script (we put it in the linked intake doc)

Happy to hop on a quick dev call if your engineers want to walk through live retry scenarios.

Best,
Marissa
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-10-01T11:03:00Z
Subject: Implementation checklist & sandbox ramp plan

Elena / Acme team —

Adding a short checklist so your PMs and devs have a concrete runway. I included owners (R = Redwood, A = Acme):

1) Sandbox provisioning (R) — provision sandbox key, postman collection, and a small test dataset. ETA: Oct 6.
2) Gateway allowlist (A) — approve Redwood IPs and create exception for sandbox consumers. ETA: Oct 8.
3) Quota & rate-fence (joint) — apply our rate_fence_template.xlsx to map consumer quotas and expected burst. Owner: A (feeds), R (validation).
4) Telemetry setup (A) — ingest x-request-id/x-trace-id into your logs; add a sampling rule for errors >=500. ETA: Oct 12.
5) Cutover rehearsal (joint) — run a staged traffic ramp on Oct 18 with 25%, 50%, 100% checks and rollback checklist.
6) Rollback plan (R) — revert DNS to pre-cutover gateway handler and re-enable token-level throttles; we will keep a warm fallback model for 48 hours post-cutover.

Operational knobs and thresholds we recommend during ramp:
- Keep client retry max at 3 during ramp, raise after stabilization.
- Watch for gateway 429 ratio >0.5% — hold ramp and increase tokens.
- If 5xx rate exceeds 1% for 10 minutes, trigger automated rollback.

Action items assigned:
- Samir (Acme): confirm sandbox contact list (samir@acme.com) — owner A
- Platform-ops (Acme): confirm gateway exception and quota mappings — owner A
- Marissa (Redwood): send Postman collection + short smoke test scripts — owner R (ETA Oct 3)
- Jonas (Redwood): schedule cutover rehearsal with stakeholders — owner R

Attachments: rate_fence_template.xlsx (see sheet 'production-mapping')

Thanks — Monica
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference

Locking Oct 18 rehearsal — calendar invite to follow. Quick ops runbook snippet for your on-call:

1) Monitor: 5xx rate, 429 rate, avg latency (95th). If 5xx >1% for 10m -> trigger incident playbook.
2) Triage: check x-trace-id for recent failed requests and look for common error class (timeout vs server error).
3) Immediate mitigation (5–10 min): pause ramp, reduce client concurrency by 50%, switch to fallback model endpoint (we'll provide endpoint alias), and escalate to Platform-ops.
4) Rollback (if unresolved after 20m): redirect traffic to previous gateway entry (DNS rollback) and re-enable pre-cutover throttles. Notify execs and start postmortem.

We'll send Postman collection, a small smoke test script, and the live retry template to Samir by EOD.

Jonas
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
